text:
Florida arrives on the second night of a back-to-back, still stinging from a 5-1 loss at OTT that ended a three-game winning streak. The Panthers are also without Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov, with Carter Verhaeghe now skating beside Sam Reinhart and Matthew Tkachuk. Pittsburgh has lost four straight (0-4-0) after a 5-4 defeat at UTA, and is missing Bryan Rust and Ben Kindel. Blake Lizotte is next in line for Kindel's minutes. The chances say the slide is real: the Penguins have taken just 44% of the expected goals (the quality of shots) in those four games.

The model sees an even game, 3.2 expected goals for FLA and 3.15 for PIT. Florida has the better chance profile at five on five, giving up 2.91 expected goals per 60 to Pittsburgh's 3.55. But the Panthers take six penalties a game, and that hands the other side power plays. Neither projected goalie inspires confidence. Akira Schmid (FLA) is at -3.1 goals saved above expected this season, meaning he has let in about three more than an average goalie would have on those shots. Arturs Silovs (PIT) is at -1.3 this season and -12.8 last year.

Matthew Tkachuk brings a nine-game point streak and a 71% chance at a point. Brady Tkachuk is one of Ice Sheet's under-the-radar picks: he plays about 16 minutes a night on the third line, but his shots have been dangerous, with 4.8 expected goals over his last 10 games, and PIT allow the sixth-most expected goals per 60. We have him at 33% to score. For Pittsburgh, Sidney Crosby is at 32% to score, and Tommy Novak is one assist from 100 for his career.
